ordering_facts: A Branch terminalizes its path: nothing may follow it, and the paths are never rejoined.
A nested Branch is not a legal Branch-path terminal.
Nesting is bounded at two control levels. That is a bound of this contract, not a Boomi platform limit.
Paths execute in the authored order, one fully before the next.
entries.subject: branch
entries.summary: Runs 2-25 paths in the authored order, SEQUENTIALLY — never at once. Each path receives an independent copy of the document stream.
entries.title: Branch

ordering_facts: A cache read with no preceding write on the same path is reported unless an external writer is declared.
entries.subject: cache_get
entries.summary: All-document cache read. external_writer declares that the cache is populated outside this process, which is what makes a read with no in-process writer legitimate.
entries.title: Cache get

ordering_facts: A trailing cache_put belongs in a Branch path terminal (the staging shape), not in the step list.
entries.subject: cache_put
entries.summary: Writes the stream into a document cache and CONSUMES it: a cache_put in a step position must be followed immediately by a stream-replacing cache read.
entries.title: Cache put (add to cache)

ordering_facts: Removal acts on the cache, not on the document stream flowing through this path.
entries.subject: cache_remove
entries.summary: Removes ALL documents from a cache. Keyed removal is capability-gated.
entries.title: Cache remove

ordering_facts: An action whose row produces no documents is terminal: nothing may consume what it did not return.
Whether a call may open a path, and whether anything may follow it, comes from its family/action row, not from its position.
Whether a call may sit inside a retried region comes from its replay classification; no caller-supplied evidence can lift a refusal.
entries.subject: connector_call
entries.summary: A first-class connector call. Authors ONLY the operation reference — the connection is derived from the component plan, because a connector-action component does not declare its own connection. The optional action is an assertion of intent, never an override.
entries.title: Connector call

ordering_facts: Operations run in the authored order and each one's stream effect applies to the next.
Splitting and combining documents is not the same as joining control paths; this contract emits no path join at all.
entries.subject: data_process
entries.summary: One or more explicit operations run in the authored order: custom scripting, split_documents, combine_documents. Document fan-out and fan-in are authored here and nowhere else.
entries.title: Data process

ordering_facts: A Decision terminalizes its path: nothing may follow it, and the arms are never rejoined.
Nesting is bounded at two control levels — a bound of this contract, not a Boomi platform limit.
Where the arms would converge, only state written on BOTH is established.
entries.subject: decision
entries.summary: A two-way conditional over seven comparisons. Exactly one arm runs. The two arms admit DIFFERENT bodies.
entries.title: Decision

ordering_facts: Retrieval is all-document; keyed or indexed retrieval is capability-gated.
entries.subject: document_cache_retrieve
entries.summary: Legacy all-document cache read. Replaces the stream with the cached documents.
entries.title: Document cache retrieve

ordering_facts: An exception terminates its path; nothing may follow it.
entries.subject: exception
entries.summary: Terminal throw. The message template must carry the {1} placeholder whenever parameter_source binds a value.
entries.title: Exception

ordering_facts: A flow control never makes a path run concurrently.
Batching regroups the stream; it never splits or combines document contents — those are explicit data_process operations.
entries.subject: flow_control
entries.summary: Batches the stream into groups of for_each_count documents. This is the only authorable flow-control mode: there is no caller-configurable parallel chunking or multiprocess execution.
entries.title: Flow control (batching)

ordering_facts: A map between two connector calls must take the earlier call's output profile and produce the later call's input profile.
A map's property effects are unknown unless a typed effect contract declares them, so state written only inside a map is not established.
entries.subject: map_ref
entries.summary: Applies a map component to the stream. Source and destination profiles live in the map component and are never authored here.
entries.title: Map reference

ordering_facts: A message produces its own document, so it does not pass the inbound one through.
entries.subject: message
entries.summary: Replaces the stream with one document built from the authored text.
entries.title: Message

ordering_facts: A process call may not share a root-to-leaf path with a connector call while that combination is capability-gated; sibling paths are independent and do not count as sharing.

Nothing may follow a process call. Author it as the terminal of its path, with no steps before it in that body and no stop after it; a root sequence containing a call holds that call and nothing else.
To run several children, give each its own path — separate branch paths, or separate wrappers — rather than chaining calls.
entries.subject: process_call
entries.summary: Invokes another process by opaque reference, and ENDS the path it is on: whether execution continues past a call is decided by the called process, which hands control back only through the return-document steps it declares, so this version supports the non-returning form only. wait=false returns immediately and therefore establishes no downstream state.
entries.title: Process call

ordering_facts: Admitted in the root sequence only — not in a Branch path, a Decision arm, or a Try/Catch body.
Returns and terminates; nothing may follow it.
entries.subject: return_documents
entries.summary: Terminal that hands the current batch back to the caller. A plain stop ends the path without returning anything.
entries.title: Return documents

ordering_facts: Steps execute in the authored order, top to bottom.
The root sequence must reach a terminal; an unterminated path is rejected.
entries.subject: sequence
entries.summary: The ordered body of the process. Steps run in the authored order, and the last one must be a terminal — every path ends explicitly.
entries.title: Sequence (process body)

ordering_facts: Per-document state is not visible across sibling paths: each path receives its own copy of the documents.
Where paths converge, only state written on every incoming path is established.
entries.subject: set_ddp
entries.summary: Writes a per-document property. The name is BARE — the wire prefix is owned by emission. Source values concatenate in the authored order.
entries.title: Set dynamic document property

ordering_facts: Per-execution state accumulates across Branch paths in the authored order, so a later path sees what an earlier one wrote.
Reading in an earlier path what a later path writes is rejected; reordering the paths is the fix.
entries.subject: set_dpp
entries.summary: Writes a per-execution property. The name is BARE. persist changes durability, never scope.
entries.title: Set dynamic process property

ordering_facts: A source occupies the first position of the sequence it opens.
It takes no inbound documents. What it RETURNS is decided by its family/action row, not by the node.
entries.subject: source
entries.summary: The entry connector call of a legacy linear process. Authors both the connection and the operation reference; the compiler derives connector metadata from the resolved components.
entries.title: Source endpoint

ordering_facts: A Branch path or Decision true arm ending in a stop must do some work first; a Decision false arm may stop with no steps at all.
A stop terminates its path; nothing may follow it.
entries.subject: stop
entries.summary: Plain successful terminal. Ends the path and returns nothing.
entries.title: Stop

ordering_facts: A target is a legal terminal of a Branch path and of a Decision true arm; it is not admitted on a Decision false arm.
It consumes inbound documents. Whether it RETURNS any is decided by its family/action row — a database Send returns nothing, a REST PATCH does.
On the legacy linear path a target is immediately followed by a stop.
entries.subject: target
entries.summary: A routed destination connector call. Authors both the connection and the operation reference.
entries.title: Target endpoint

ordering_facts: Both paths terminate independently; nothing may follow a try_catch.
Retry over an action classified non_idempotent or unverified is refused outright, whatever evidence is attached.
Try/Catch does not nest: composition would rewrite the outer handler's effective error selection.
Typed idempotency evidence only discharges the obligation on an action already classified idempotent_write or conditionally_idempotent.
entries.subject: try_catch
entries.summary: A scoped error handler. A process scope must be the sole root step; a connector scope must follow the call that produced the documents. Retry count is 0-5, the platform's own bound.
entries.title: Try/Catch with bounded retry

entries.subject: branch.path_order
entries.summary: Paths are sequential, never concurrent, and per-execution state written in an earlier path is visible in a later one. Ordering is therefore part of the design, not a detail of it.
entries.title: Branch paths run in the authored order

entries.subject: control.depth_bound
entries.summary: A bound of this compiler, NOT a Boomi platform limit. Deeper routing belongs in a subprocess reached by a process call.
entries.title: Control nesting is bounded at two levels

entries.subject: control.no_continuation
entries.summary: Nothing may follow a Branch or a Decision, and their outlets are never rejoined. Work that must happen afterwards is authored inside every path or arm.
entries.title: Control nodes terminalize their path

entries.subject: documents.explicit_split_combine
entries.summary: Fan-out and fan-in are authored data_process operations. No control node and no flow control changes document cardinality implicitly.
entries.title: Splitting and combining documents is always explicit

entries.subject: references.opaque
entries.summary: References are authored as '$ref:KEY' tokens or literal component ids. Connector families, actions, credentials, configuration and profiles are never authored alongside them — the compiler resolves them from the component plan.
entries.title: Every component reference is opaque

entries.subject: retry.replay_safety
entries.summary: Retry over an action classified non_idempotent or unverified is refused outright regardless of evidence. Typed evidence only discharges the extra obligation on an action already classified idempotent_write (verified_action) or conditionally_idempotent (key_reference resolving to the same operation).
entries.title: Replay safety is decided by the action, not by the caller

entries.subject: state.convergence
entries.summary: The meet over converging paths is intersection, not union: state written on one arm only is not established after the arms converge.
entries.title: Converging paths keep only what both established
